title: Calculating the Mean When Data Exist

blocks.text: Total divided by the number of elements

The arithmetic mean is the sum of the values divided by the number of values. The denominator is not the last index: a four-element vector has size four and last index three. Nor is it the number of distinct values: every observation counts, even if the same magnitude occurs more than once.

First, check whether data exist. If the collection is empty, this formula does not define a mean because the denominator would be zero. We display a message indicating that no mean is available. To preserve fractional results, convert the quantities to double before dividing.
Here, seven divided by two produces 3.5. Conversion happens before division. We will keep integer sums small; double does not make an overflow that already happened while adding into an int safe.

blocks.question: Why don't we assign a mean of zero to an empty collection by default?
options: Because observations equal to zero are excluded from the data count.
Because having no data is not equivalent to a valid mean of zero.
Because calculating a mean requires at least two observations.
blocks.explanation: Every observation counts, even if it is zero. The collection {0} has one observation and a mean of zero; an empty collection has no observations and no positive denominator. The No mean message preserves that distinction.

blocks.question: Predict the exact output, without adding quotation marks.
blocks.explanation: Converting before dividing preserves both the sign and the fractional part of a negative total.

blocks.text: size() returns an unsigned size. We will not directly mix a negative int sum with that size in integer division: conversions between types could change the calculation's meaning. Explicitly converting both quantities to double makes the intended representation clear in this formula.

blocks.question: You want a fractional mean. Which sequence preserves the information?
options: Convert the quantities to double before division and check that data exist.
Change only the result's name to decimal.
Divide two integers and convert the quotient afterward.
blocks.explanation: The timing of the conversion matters and does not replace checking for an empty collection.

blocks.text: For fractional measurements, we can use std::vector<double> and a double accumulator from the start. The values and their sum still have finite precision. We choose simple data so the traversal and mean are easy to reason about; short displayed output does not guarantee exactness for every measurement.

blocks.text: If the question asks for the mean of selected values, the denominator is the number of selected values, not the size of the original collection. No values may be selected even when the original collection contains elements. We must check that second empty case before division.

options: Divide zero by three and call it the selected mean.

blocks.explanation: A nonempty source does not guarantee a nonempty subset.
